answer: knoll folds wallets and hosts under shared control into one history and signs a single epoch clock for its vault. After each admission, the next head must age that vault for its ordinal in attested epochs, with one jade locked throughout; admission spends the age. Ten heads cost 55 serial epochs of lockup on that jade, the tenth costing ten. Extra keys cannot run separate clocks or divide the lock, while an unrelated operator’s first head costs one epoch.
